content: {"like": ["The best moments of the opera remain moving and frequently beautiful"], "dislike": ["The director’s attempt to impose contemporary Palestinian/Israeli conflict onto Rossini’s opera is absurd and inappropriate", "The production’s use of violence, blood, dead children, and photographs of missing persons is offensive and irrelevant", "The inclusion of computers, filming, kitschy Egyptian statues, and an enamel gold throne creates an incongruous and chaotic stage", "The political agenda imposed on the opera betrays Rossini’s original intent and makes the music seem irrelevant, arbitrary, and trivial", "The overburdened production and excessive recitative detract from the opera’s quality", "The overall post‑modern approach is seen as vanity and a betrayal of the true creators"]}
